assessments.reasoning: The §5.5.1.2.1 category lists at pp.117–118 map the named source and destination types to the finite, in-range floating/fixed-point to integral row. The §5.5.1.2.1.1 tie rule then selects the even nearest integer in that row.

challenge.method: Check the input and destination type classifications separately. Challenge with negative half-way values, NaN, infinity, a value outside the destination range, and the neighboring row for conversion to floating or fixed-point destinations. Recompute ties independently as arithmetic examples.
challenge.results: Other input classes, non-finite or overflowing data, and nonintegral destinations are outside the selected row. Integer rounding of −2.5, −1.5, 1.5, 2.5 and 3.5 yields −2, −2, 2, 2 and 4. Those arithmetic checks verify the named tie interpretation and are not observations of a VBA implementation.

limitations: This judgment applies to the exact May 20, 2025 MS-VBAL revision 2.4. The publisher currently lists a later edition. Its requirements and behavior of any Office host are outside this review.
The claim requires an otherwise valid coercion from a finite in-range value to an integral declared type.
